Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Mn to Scale AI Agents for Restaurant Businesses
Om Singh
| November 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million in funding from Houston-based Narahari Investments as it looks to expand its artificial intelligence solutions for restaurant businesses.
The fresh capital will support the expansion of its AI Catering Sales Agent, the launch of three additional AI agents currently in beta testing, and the development of a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.
Founded in December 2025 by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy , Kutlerri.ai is developing AI-powered tools to help restaurants generate more sales, control operating expenses and improve profitability. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.
Unlike conventional software providers that charge fixed subscription fees, Kutlerri.ai follows a performance-linked pricing model. Restaurants are charged based on the additional revenue generated or costs saved through its products.
AI Agent Helps Restaurants Find Catering Customers
Kutlerri.ai’s first commercially available product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, focuses on helping restaurants grow their catering businesses.
The agent identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius of a restaurant and reaches out to them through emails, text messages and phone calls. It also helps restaurants convert incoming enquiries into catering orders.
The product was developed in collaboration with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group operating in the Washington DC region.
According to Kutlerri.ai, its AI agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over a 10-month period. The startup said the revenue was more than 10 times the amount RASA paid for the service, without requiring the restaurant group to hire additional sales personnel.
Plans to Expand Product Portfolio and Team
Kutlerri.ai currently has one commercially available product, three AI agents undergoing beta testing and two more in development.
The latest funding will help the company accelerate product development, expand its teams and bring additional AI-powered solutions to restaurant operators.
The startup has more than 10 signed customers in the US, which remains its primary market. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also maintains an office in Houston.
Alongside its US expansion, Kutlerri.ai is exploring business opportunities in India and other markets.

articles.title: MetaX and UBTech-backed robotics chip startup Xilect raises RMB 500 million
articles.snippet: MetaX and UBTech-backed robotics chip startup Xilect raises RMB 500 million TechNode
articles.text:
Xilect, a robotics chip startup jointly founded by Chinese GPU maker MetaX and humanoid robot maker UBTech Robotics, has raised RMB 500 million in an angel round. The company will use the funding to develop its first chip and supporting software, expand its engineering team and test the platform with robot manufacturers.
Xilect is designing a system-on-chip that combines multimodal perception, decision-making and motion control on the robot itself. Its software toolchain is intended to help robot makers run existing AI models on the platform. The startup plans to give partners a development and testing platform in 2027 and release its first chip in 2028. [ Xilect , in Chinese]

Backswing Ventures Announces Investment in Ukrainian Defense Technology Company Vigilant Works
News provided by
Backswing Ventures
Nov 12, 2026, 08:30 ET
Share this article
Share this article
ORLANDO, Fla. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Backswing Ventures, the defense venture capital firm, today announced its investment in Vigilant Works , a Ukrainian defense technology company developing autonomous counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS), high-speed interceptor platforms, and radar-based detection capabilities designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Continue Reading
Backswing Ventures logo
The investment will support Vigilant Works' continued development of its autonomous guidance technologies, next-generation radar capabilities, and expansion of its operations as the company prepares to scale production and establish a broader presence across NATO-allied countries.
Backswing Ventures invests selectively in companies addressing critical challenges across defense and national security. As aerial threats continue to evolve in speed, sophistication, and scale, the ability to detect, track, and intercept them autonomously is becoming increasingly important. Vigilant Works is developing an integrated approach to counter-UAS operations, combining high-speed interception, autonomous guidance, and radar technology into a scalable defense ecosystem.
Founded by a team of engineers and defense technology entrepreneurs, Vigilant Works is developing an autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem combining interceptor platforms, proprietary autonomy technologies, and radar-based detection capabilities. Its first-generation Algiz-1 has undergone battlefield testing, providing operational experience that informs the development of its next-generation systems. The company is currently advancing Algiz-2, a next-generation interceptor capable of speeds exceeding 600 km/h and designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Vigilant Works has recently entered active battlefield testing of Algiz-2 and secured its first commercial agreements outside Ukraine. The company is also developing its proprietary autonomy stack and radar solutions in Ukraine, with investment capital supporting continued technology development and preparations to scale production and operations across NATO-allied countries. The company is a member of Brave1, Ukraine's defense technology coordination platform, and was previously selected for the Brave1 / Ministry of Defence EU4UA program.
"We are excited to support Vigilant Works as they continue developing and scaling their autonomous defense capabilities," said Kyle Asman , Managing Partner at Backswing Ventures. "The evolution of aerial threats is creating an increasingly urgent need for effective counter-UAS solutions. Vigilant Works has the benefit of developing its technology in an environment where these capabilities are being tested against real operational requirements. We believe the team's focus on autonomous interception, radar, and high-speed threats addresses an important and growing need across the defense ecosystem."
"We believe the next leap in counter-UAS will come from rethinking the entire interception chain, much like rocketry did decades ago. Detection, radar, autonomy, and high-speed interception cannot be developed in isolation.
